description: Square four-post canopy module roofed in corrugated metal sheeting on a welded steel frame, single slope, open on all sides.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post canopy module with a single-slope roof of corrugated metal sheeting, welded steel angle frame and four square steel posts at the corners, open on all sides Materials: Galvanised corrugated steel sheet with chalky white oxidation and rust blooming along the sheet overlaps and screw lines, red-oxide primer showing through scuffed and dented steel posts.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.94. 3,188/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Turntable passes at every azimuth with holed=false and an enclosed-background fraction of 0.0005 to 0.0074 against the gate ceiling of 0.01, so it is run WITHOUT --allow-holes.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 2.900 x 4.000 m off the built module, the deck owning both cell-edge planes and the frame stopping at 1.988, so check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m. Four 120 x 58 mm channel posts at +-1.928 under a 200 mm perimeter beam that is itself a CHANNEL -- an 8 mm web recessed between a 12 mm top and bottom flange on all four sides, where the first build had a plain slab -- and a SINGLE plane falling 2.90 at -Z to 2.40 at +Z. The declared 2.90 is the top of the crests and the crest that sets it is the DEEPENED one at a sheet lap, standing 1.8 amplitudes proud; authored off the ordinary crest it stood at 2.905 and the bay was over its own envelope.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy reads the footprint as rectangular at 0.858:1; the notes fix a square 4 m cell and govern. Everything under the sheet now hangs from the underside of its TROUGHS rather than its mean plane, so the beam's top flange and the purlins no longer stand 18 and 3 mm up into the corrugation valleys and show through them.

featureReviews.evidence: 52 modelled flutes 36 mm deep across the 4 m in FOUR courses of 1.00 m -- the real cover width of a sheet -- with the lap flute at columns 26, 52 and 78 standing 1.8 amplitudes proud, so both the eave and the rake are a sawtooth and the three interior seams the plate shows are all in frame. The first build lapped every 20 flutes from column 0, so one of its three landed ON the rake and only two were ever seen. Each course carries its own tone (1.000 / 0.958 / 1.032 / 0.974), there is a 0.11 m rusted band along the eave and both rakes, and two lines of 13 screw washers sit on the crests over the purlins. Measured on MATCHED WINDOWS entirely inside the deck -- plate 280..760 x 150..300 (n 72,000), render 300..720 x 280..420 (n 58,800) -- the plate reads mean 187.8, sd 26.1, p05 144.0, p50 187.4, p95 229.2 and the shipped deck reads mean 196.8, sd 22.3, p05 151.3, p50 201.9, p95 221.6 -- 85% of the plate's spread. The first build read 193.7 / 195.6 / 227.8 at saturation 0.007 to 0.021: the right tone and effectively one colour.
featureReviews.notes: 2,516 triangles for the deck and 3,188 for the bay, against the registry notes' prediction that modelled flutes would eat the whole budget. The canvas ripple is phase-locked to the geometry at 13 per metre in both, with a trough at x = 0 in both.

featureReviews.evidence: Channel section built as a web and two flanges per post with the WEB darker than the flanges it sits between (the plate's #5c2c28 against #78342e, about 0.79 in linear terms; the first build had it the brighter of the two and a channel read as a bar). BOTH materials are envelope re-based, so a chalk bloom can land brighter than the clean tone a multiply could only darken. Measured over the POSTS ALONE -- the rows below the beam soffit, where nothing up-facing is in frame -- the front view runs mean 51.5, p05 44.2, p50 49.0, p95 68.2 and the back view mean 38.8, p05 31.0, p50 35.1, p95 55.6, against a plate whose posts sit at 28.6, 38.7, 54.1, 66.0, 67.4 and 72.0. The first build rendered three separate posts and every face of them at exactly #a33123, luma 72.2.
featureReviews.notes: The world UV scale is set by the post and not chosen: at 0.80 m a 0.12 m post crossed 15% of one tile and every post crossed the same 15%; at 0.40 m the strip repeated six times down each post as a chevron ladder; at 1.10 m it is two repeats and the y tint carries the rest.

name: Corrugated Metal Canopy Module
nameTh: หลังคาสังกะสี
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; placed side by side the posts pair up at the shared edges, which is what a real market row looks like rather than a defect to design out. Single slope rather than gabled -- a lean-to shed roof is what corrugated sheet is actually built as here -- running 2.4 m at the low eave to 2.9 m at the high, so bays butted along the fall continue one plane and bays butted across it step. Open on all sides. The corrugation profile is a normal map on a flat deck, never modelled flutes: at 4 m across, modelled corrugations would eat the whole triangle budget for a ripple a normal map carries exactly.
